newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Clabecq says restructuring going ahead.
newsitem.headline: Clabecq says restructuring going ahead.

text.p: Loss-making Belgian steel maker Forges de Clabecq SA said on Tuesday it was continuing with a restructuring plan while awaiting news from the European Commission on a recapitalisation project for the company.

"Work is going ahead as normal in the factory - production is flat out," Clabecq's chief executive Libert Froidmont told Reuters. "Obviously, we are busy putting into place the restructuring and reorganisation plan for the company.
European Commission sources said earlier the Commission was to start a formal probe on Wednesday into a rescue plan for the troubled steel maker.

Belgium's Walloon region -- Clabecq's main shareholder -- forwarded the plan to the Commission in June. It involves a 1.5-billion-franc capital injection into Clabecq which has monthly debt and other charges of around 70 million francs.
Under the European Coal and Steel Community Treaty, state aid for the steel industry, suffering from overcapacity, can only be allowed in very exceptional cases.
The Commission was also querying a bridging loan of 200 million francs already paid to the company and a proposal to write off debts of 500 million francs, one source said.
Froidmont said he was as yet unaware of precisely what the European authorities thought of the recapitalisation project.
"When I know, I will see what attitude to take," he said.
He added that of the 700 job losses announced under the restructuring plan from a workforce of 2,143 people, 350 departures had already taken place or were foreseen.
